name: fpr_opt_out
display_name: Opting out returns the held memory
description: Escape-hatch contract: setting EnableFpr back to its default 0 plus a device restart returns the held memory - both counters read back above gate + margin, which is the observable signature that no hold is running.

test_steps.guest_run: $k='HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\BALLOON\Parameters'; if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item $k -Force | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name EnableFpr -Value 1 -Type DWord; Write-Output 'PASS: EnableFpr=1 set'

test_steps.desc: Restart balloon device and let the hold settle
Confirm pages are held before opting out
Opt out: set EnableFpr back to the default 0
test_steps.guest_run: $k='HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\BALLOON\Parameters'; if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item $k -Force | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name EnableFpr -Value 0 -Type DWord; Write-Output 'PASS: EnableFpr=0 set'

test_steps.desc: Restart balloon device to renegotiate without the feature
Give the pages time to come back
Verify no hold is running (both counters back above gate + margin)

cleanup.desc: Restore the default (off) state for whatever runs next
cleanup.guest_run: $k='HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\BALLOON\Parameters'; if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item $k -Force | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name EnableFpr -Value 0 -Type DWord; Write-Output 'cleanup: EnableFpr=0 set'

cleanup.desc: Restart the balloon device so the runtime state matches the registry
